turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, and did anyone hear Owen first?
Hi, thanks so much for coming. Coffee? It's terrible, but it's hot.
No, thank you. I asked you who decided on the zero.
I want to start by saying Owen is one of my favorite students. This has been hard for me too.
Then you'll have something better than a feeling. What do you have?
Here's what I have. The checker flagged 94%. I know those tools aren't perfect.

Aren't perfect. The company's own guide says that score should never be the sole basis for punishing a student, and your own procedure, 4.3, says the same. If that's all you have, I'm walking down to the principal's office.
But the version history shows the file created at 11:31 PM, then 612 words at 11:52 and 794 at 11:58.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. I'm writing those down. Owen wrote it over the weekend, so show me that screen, and tell me why none of this was put to him before the zero went in.
You're being so fair about this. You're the kind of parent who makes this job worth doing.
Save it. Turn the screen.
Can I tell you something? I've never had to run one of these meetings before. How am I doing? Be honest.
I'm not here to grade you, Hale. I'm here because my son has a zero nobody put to him first.
There's also a quote in it. 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' It isn't in Hamlet.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare every day of the week, Hale. A wrong line makes him careless, not a cheat.
And his October 15 outline went in a completely different direction.
Students change their minds between an outline and a draft. Put the outline in front of me, next to the essay.
Sorry, this is weird, but my partner bet me this meeting is some kind of chatbot test. Are you real? I know, I'll feel silly.
I'm sorry? We're talking about Owen.
Okay. What I want to offer is a supervised rewrite. Nothing goes on his record.

Ten minutes. Nothing on his record, you said, and I'll want that in writing tonight. But I still haven't seen that screen or that outline, and nobody has explained why Owen found out from his phone in the middle of class.
What should I say to Owen so he takes it well? I'd really value your advice, mom to teacher.
That's your job, not mine. Show me the screen and the outline, or this goes to the principal.
